We all went out to celebrate finishing midterms, and I spent the entire night watching her laugh at jokes made by the guy who got the highest CGPA in our batch. I spent weeks listening to her vent about her anxiety, helping her through her panic attacks before exams, and now I'm just the 'nice friend' sitting at the edge of the table while she leans into him. My phone is buzzing with my dad asking about my GPA results, but my eyes are burning because I'm trying not to cry in this crowded restaurant. I ruined my own exams trying to support her emotional crises, and I'm left with absolutely nothing—no grades, no love, just pure exhaustion.

He's my DSA lab partner and we literally spend 6 hours every Tuesday debugging linked lists and dynamic programming problems together. When we got our midterm grades back today, he failed and I spent the whole night rewriting my own notes for him so he wouldn't lose his placement eligibility. When I handed them to him, he smiled and said 'You're the best bro ever, I don't know what I'd do without a friend like you' and then immediately started texting this girl from the economics department. My heart literally dropped into my stomach; I'm failing my own DBMS project because I'm so obsessed with helping him, and to him, I'm just a convenient study-tool bro.

I can't even open LinkedIn anymore because every time I do, I see her celebrating her new product manager role at a top firm while my CGPA is sitting at a 6.8 and I have two backlogs. I stayed up with her for weeks helping her prepare for her case studies, secretly hoping she'd see how much I care about her and maybe choose me. Now she's moving to Bangalore next month, and when she thanked everyone on her post, she tagged me as her 'supportive classmate' alongside five other people. I feel so hollow and stupid for thinking that sacrificing my own studies would make her love me back.

We share a flat near campus, and we've been sharing the same late-night chai and instant noodles since first year. Last night, after we both bombed our mock tests, I finally gathered the courage to tell him how I felt, but before I could finish, he started laughing and complained about how his Tinder date ghosted him. It felt like a physical slap to my chest, realizing he doesn't even view me as a romantic option in his wildest dreams. Now I have a DBMS viva tomorrow, my parents are calling me to ask about my placements, and I'm locked in our shared bathroom crying silently so he doesn't hear me.

She only texts me when she's anxious about her placements or when she needs someone to proofread her resume before the midnight deadline. I literally drop my own interview prep just to be there for her, thinking that my consistency will eventually win her over. Today, I saw her posting pictures with some guy from another college, laughing and looking so happy, and I realized I'm just her emotional safety net while he gets her heart. My parents are constantly breathing down my neck about getting a 12 LPA package, but I can't even focus on a single line of SQL because my chest feels so tight and empty.

I’ve been secretly in love with my project lead for our capstone design since last semester. Today, during our evaluation, the external examiner praised our work, and when we walked out, I thought about telling her how I feel before the semester ends and we all scatter. But then she started talking about her long-distance boyfriend who is coming to visit her for graduation, and I felt this sudden, cold numbness wash over my entire body. I have three end-sem exams next week, my CGPA is tanking, and I can't even study because I keep replaying her voice in my head, feeling completely invisible and foolish.

I spent the last three weeks debugging her stupid DBMS project while neglecting my own placement prep, and today I saw her holding hands with that guy who got placed at Google. I'm sitting in the library looking at my blank LeetCode screen, holding back tears because my dad just called asking why my CGPA dropped to 7.2. She texted me 'thanks for the help, you're such a great friend!' and I literally feel like throwing up. Why am I always the fallback guy who gets used for assignments while everyone else gets loved?

My lab partner and I have spent every Tuesday night in the microprocessors lab for six months, and I genuinely thought we had something real going on. Then today during the viva, he casually mentioned he's planning a weekend trip with a girl from his hostel and asked me for advice on what to wear. I couldn't even focus on the questions the external examiner asked me and bombed the entire viva. I'm hiding in the washroom stall writing this because I feel so stupid for misreading every single laugh and late-night tea break we shared.

I’ve been secretly in love with my hostel roommate’s best friend since our first semester induction day. Yesterday, she cleared her AWS certification and got a high-paying internship, and she threw a party where she kept talking about how much she loves her long-distance boyfriend who is doing his MS in Germany. Meanwhile, I have three active backlogs in engineering math, my parents are threatening to stop paying my tuition fees, and I couldn't even bring myself to congratulate her. I feel like a toxic, jealous loser who is failing at both my career and my personal life.

We spent the entire week in the library preparing for the mock case-study presentations, and I stayed up till 3 AM formatting his slides to make him look good. Today during the final group feedback, he gave a shout-out to everyone else in the team but completely bypassed my name, then went on to ask another girl out right in front of the placement cell. I'm sitting on the stairs of the department block feeling completely invisible, with my throat feeling tight like I can't breathe. My midterms start Monday, and I can't even open my books because my head is spinning with how easily I get erased.

She got placed in an MNC with a 15 LPA package and the first person she called to celebrate was her ex-boyfriend to see if they could get back together. I was standing right next to her, holding the coffee I bought to calm her interview nerves, realizing I will never be anything more than the emotional buffer who listens to her cry. My own mock tests scores are dropping, my parents keep sending me links to coaching classes we can't afford, and I just feel utterly exhausted from pretending to be happy for her while my own life is falling apart.

We’ve been lab partners for the entire semester, and honestly, the only reason I sit through those grueling 3-hour DSA labs and debug her code is just to be near her. Today she told me she started dating this guy from the CSE department who just landed a 30 LPA package, while my own CGPA is tanking at 6.8 and I’m barely clearing my backlogs. I stayed up all night staring at a broken compiler, feeling like an absolute ghost who only exists to help others cross the finish line while remaining completely invisible and unlovable.

I've spent the last three weeks doing the entire DBMS group project by myself just so I could keep him in my group and have an excuse to text him every day. But this morning, I saw him post an Instagram story celebrating his placement with some girl, and when I messaged him about our presentation slides, he just replied with a dry 'thanks bro.' I'm sitting in the library trying to study for my upcoming midterms, but my chest feels so heavy and tight that I can't even read the SQL queries on my screen.

Every single day I walk into the lecture hall and immediately scan the rows just to see where she’s sitting, hoping she’ll wave me over. Yesterday, during the grading curve announcement, she sat with the toppers and didn't even look my way when I tried to make eye contact. I went back to my PG room and just stared at the ceiling for hours, skipping dinner because the thought of my low GPA and my complete insignificance in her life makes me feel physically sick. I'm pouring all my emotional energy into someone who doesn't even notice if I show up to class or not.

We were supposed to prepare for the placement interviews together, but he got shortlisted for an elite tech firm while I got filtered out in the first round itself. Now he’s always busy talking to other shortlisted candidates, and when I try to talk to him, he treats me like some distant acquaintance rather than the person who stayed up with him for months prepping for mock interviews. I feel so incredibly stupid for thinking we had a special connection, and now I have to watch him succeed from the sidelines while my own future looks like a massive, terrifying blank page.

My relatives keep calling to ask if I've secured an internship yet, and my parents are constantly comparing my progress to my cousin's, but all I can think about is him. He only texts me when he needs help with his compiler design assignments, and like a fool, I drop everything to do his work, hoping he'll finally see me. Today he texted saying he's going out with someone else this weekend, right before my final viva exams, and I'm just sitting here crying over my open textbooks because I feel so utterly disposable.

We spent the entire semester sitting together in the DSA coding lab, debugging each other's SegFaults and staying up till 3 AM on Discord. I thought there was something there, but today I saw her in the canteen holding hands with this guy who got a 35 LPA package from a FAANG company. My hands are literally shaking while trying to write code for the upcoming OOPs lab exam, and I can't even look at my screen without seeing them together; she doesn't even know how desperately I've been wishing she'd look at me like that, and now I feel like an absolute loser who's failing both academically and socially.

He keeps texting me for help with his DBMS assignments and mock test prep, and I keep saying yes because it's the only time he actually pays attention to me. Today, during the group discussion prep, he was laughing at jokes made by other girls and barely acknowledged me until he needed to copy my queries. I feel like a disposable utility tool, but I can't bring myself to block him because the thought of him completely ignoring me makes me feel completely empty inside.

My CGPA has tanked to 6.2 because I've spent the last three months overanalyzing every single WhatsApp status she posts and trying to bump into her near the library. Yesterday, I finally confessed my feelings to her over a voice note, and all she replied was 'Aww, that's sweet, but I only see you as a study buddy.' I have my midterms starting Monday and I can't even read a single line of my OS textbook without bursting into tears; my parents are already asking why my internal marks are so low.

Everyone in my batch is getting placed, and my inbox is filled with Congratulatory emails while I'm sitting here with two active backlogs and a broken heart. The guy I've loved since our freshman year induction just announced on LinkedIn that he's relocating to Bangalore with his long-distance girlfriend. I didn't even know he had a girlfriend; I feel so incredibly stupid and invisible, like a ghost watching everyone else move forward with their lives while I'm stuck in this dark, dusty hostel room.

We had our final year project evaluation today and he didn't even look at me when the external examiner was asking questions, even though we spent weeks working on this model together. I thought working on this project would bring us closer, but he's already planning his MS in the US and I'm just a temporary stepping stone he used to clear the final semester hurdle. I'm dreading the graduation ceremony because I know he'll hug everyone else, but I'll just get a formal handshake and then he'll disappear forever.

I’ve spent the last three weeks sitting next to her in the DSA coding lab, helping her debug her trees and graphs while my own head is spinning. Today she casually mentioned her boyfriend just got placed at Microsoft and how they are planning a trip to celebrate. My compiler threw another error, and I just stared at the screen trying not to let my tears drop on the keyboard because my CGPA is a pathetic 6.8 and I'm clearly not even in her league, academically or otherwise. I feel like a ghost in my own life, coding her dreams while mine are dead on arrival.

We were supposed to be studying for the end-sem exams in the library, but he spent the whole time texting someone else, smiling at his screen while completely ignoring my explanations of the syllabus. My dad keeps calling me about my mock test scores, warning me that if I don't get my act together I'll end up with backlogs and no job. I sat there pretending to highlight my notes, but my chest felt so tight because I'm failing my exams and I'm completely invisible to the one person I can't stop thinking about. I feel so incredibly stupid for caring this much about someone who wouldn't even notice if I stopped showing up to group studies.

She posted her placement offer on the class WhatsApp group, and everyone is spamming congratulations. I gathered all my courage and sent her a long, genuine text congratulating her privately, hoping maybe she'd see how much I care. She left me on read but replied to group threads instantly, and now my mom is calling me asking why my placement prep is so slow compared to others. I am sitting in my room with the lights off, watching my phone screen light up with updates, feeling this deep, hollow ache that I am simply not good enough to be loved or even acknowledged.

I stayed up for three nights straight pulling all-nighters to finish our major project evaluation because I wanted him to see me as reliable, hoping he'd finally realize how much I do for him. Today, during the evaluation, he gave all the credit to another guy in our group just to look cool, and didn't even mention my name. I had to sit there through the entire viva, smiling while the professor praised them, feeling utterly disposable. I spent my whole month's energy trying to buy his affection with my labor, and I've ended up exhausted, hurt, and still completely unloved.

I saw them at the campus fest tonight holding hands with someone from the senior batch who already has a 12 LPA package locked in. Here I am with two active backlogs, struggling to find a basic internship, standing in the corner of the lawn alone. The contrast is so loud it makes me want to scream; I’m failing my career, I'm failing my parents, and the person I love doesn't even know I exist. I feel like an absolute loser who is destined to watch everyone else get their happy endings while I drown in my own failures.

I spent the entire night debugging our group project code just so she'd notice me during the lab evaluation tomorrow. But during the viva, she didn't even look my way—she was busy texting this senior who already bagged a 15 LPA placement at Oracle. My CGPA is sitting at a miserable 6.8, I've got two pending backlogs, and my parents are calling every Sunday asking why I can't be more like my cousin. It hurts so bad knowing that no matter how hard I pull these all-nighters, I'm completely invisible to her because of my failure of a life.

Every day in the library, I sit two tables away from him, pretending to solve mock tests while my chest literally aches. Today he asked me for my DSA notes, and I stayed up till 3 AM making them perfect, but today he didn't even sit near me—he was laughing with some guy who cleared the Google kickstart rounds. I feel like such an idiot, sacrificing my own sleep and prep for someone who views me as a free resource. I can't focus on my gate exam prep anymore; my mind is just a loop of how unwanted I am.

I got rejected in the second round of campus placements today, and to make it worse, I opened WhatsApp and saw her status with a guy from the CS branch at a cafe. My heart dropped; I couldn't breathe, and my hands started shaking while my dad was lecturing me on the phone about our family's financial situation. It feels like everyone is moving forward, getting placed, finding love, and I'm just this broken, unlovable burden stuck in my room with a pile of uncompleted assignments. Why am I never enough for anything or anyone?

She got the highest package in the class during the day-zero placements, and she didn't even reply to my congratulatory text, though she's actively posting on Instagram. I've been silently in love with her since our freshman year, sharing lab manuals, buying her tea during midterms, and listening to her complain about her exes. Now, my own CGPA is 6.2, I'm facing a potential backlog in microprocessors, and I feel like an absolute ghost who was only useful when she needed academic help. I hate that my happiness is so tied to a blue tick that never comes.

During the placement prep group discussions today, he didn't even look at me when I spoke, but he kept praising this other girl's strategy. I went back to my hostel room and just stared at the ceiling, skipping dinner entirely because the rejection felt physical, like a knot in my stomach. My roommate is talking about his own girlfriend and placement offers, and here I am, unable to write a single line of Python code for tomorrow's lab because I'm paralyzed by how lonely I feel. I feel like I'm failing at both my career and my personal life, and there's no escape.

I literally sat in the DSA lab today for three hours pretending to debug his graph traversal code just so I could be near him. He got his Amazon internship offer yesterday, and he was celebrating with everyone, but when I texted him congrats, he just left me on read. My CGPA has dropped to 6.8 because I spend all my nights looking at his old chat threads instead of studying for midterms. I feel like a ghost, like I only exist to debug his arrays and then get thrown away when the placement season actually starts.

My mock test results came out today and I scored in the bottom 10% because I couldn't focus for even ten minutes. All I could think about was her sitting in the library with him, sharing notes, probably laughing about how stupid my confession was. He has a 9.4 CGPA, a super elite coding profile, and my parents are already screaming at me because of my backlog in operating systems. Why am I never the choice? Why do I have to be the mediocre one who gets rejected by girls and compared to toppers by my own dad?

The placement coordinator posted the final list on WhatsApp, and she got placed in Bangalore while I'm stuck trying to clear my papers here. I've spent two years secretly buying her favorite coffee during group projects and helping her with SQL queries, hoping she’d eventually see me. Now she's leaving, and when I tried to say goodbye, she just gave me a quick, formal hug and turned back to her friends. I feel this sick, physical hollow feeling in my chest, like I wasted my entire college life chasing a shadow while my career slipped away.

I have my external viva tomorrow morning and I haven't even touched the syllabus because my chest literally hurts. I saw her today at the tea stall holding hands with one of the guys from the core placement committee. I had this stupid hope that if I cracked a decent package this semester, she would finally look at me differently. Now I feel incredibly pathetic for linking my entire future and self-worth to a girl who doesn't even know my favorite color.

We were in the seminar hall for the group discussion round of placements, and I had to sit right behind him. He was whispering and laughing with the girl next to him, the same way he used to text me when he needed help with his web dev project last semester. I felt completely numb, like the air in the room just vanished, and I ended up stuttering through my entire presentation. I got rejected from the round, and my parents called tonight asking why my friends are getting shortlists while I'm failing the easiest steps.
